That file is hashed by v1 and cannot do the job unedited: the test cell and the tracks are hard-coded, and the split report has no union archive cell, no scene-disjoint subset, no small-lake stratum and no new target. §1.5 therefore contradicts §5.

findings.issue: The power table covers two of the three H1-S comparators. The claim is an intersection-union test, so its power is set by the weakest pair, and the registered kNN value is far larger. Two consequences should be on record before the stamp: the small-lake rule (MDE <= 10 against every one of the three) cannot be met at any attainable block count, and the Track N rule (> 15 against any of five comparators, kNN included) may make every Track N target descriptive.
findings.evidence: results/registry.jsonl, experiment orbit_power_dev_v4, model compare_satwq_v4_noaug, chl-a MDE80 at 87 blocks: 10.266 vs mdn_b[val-sel], 14.298 vs gbm_imagery_context[val-sel], 33.705 vs location_knn[val-sel]. Same sqrt(87/B) scaling gives about 24.2 at 169 blocks and 18.7 at 282; MDE <= 10 would need about 988 blocks. Test-S small-lake blocks are at most 91 (AquaCorr) and 212 (WQP sample-key upper bound) in orbit_testS_keycounts_20261110.json. The table's MDN_B and GBM values recompute correctly.
findings.suggested_ruling: The §1.5 table is read with a third column for location kNN (33.7 at 87 blocks, about 24 at 169 and 19 at 282, same scaling); the thresholds of §1.7 (<= 10) and §2.6 (> 15) and the words "every one of the three" and "any comparator of §2.5" are final as written, and no later addendum may change a threshold or remove a comparator from either rule.

findings.issue: The confirmatory or descriptive status of the small-lake stratum and of each Track N target is fixed after validation predictions exist. The text does not fix which arm's predictions, which validation rows or which simulation settings are used, and a descriptive declaration shrinks the Track N Holm divisor ("<= 3"). This leaves choices open after validation results are seen. §1.8 calls these items count-determined, which is not exact.
findings.evidence: Amendment lines cited. orbit_power.py uses val_row_preds.parquet with n_sim = 2000 and seeds 0/1, per model and comparator; nothing in the amendment binds these for the new cells.
findings.suggested_ruling: Each status-setting MDE is computed once by orbitv2_power.py, for every scored arm and every comparator of the family, on the validation rows of the same stratum or target in the comparator selection cell, with n_sim 2,000 and seeds 0 and 1; the largest value governs; the Track N Holm divisor stays 3 and the H2-S divisor stays 6 whatever is declared descriptive; the result is a dated addendum written before the Test-S freeze candidate.

findings.issue: Deviation from the letter of the lead ruling. The lead wrote "every learned comparator gets the same 3-init averaging, and the GBM gets 3-seed bagging". The amendment gives MDN_B 10 initialisations with two read-outs as family members, GBM 3-seed bags plus a 9-seed bag for the selected member, and compares each seed unit with the full comparator. This is at least as strict for the candidate, but it differs from the ruling and from protocol §6 and needs explicit confirmation.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/architecture_research/LEAD_DECISIONS_20261110.md lines 44-46; amendment lines 346-353; docs/preregistration/orbit_protocol.md line 289 (GBM inner-best refitted as a 5-seed ensemble). Family sizes from §3.5: MDN_B 3 x 3 x 2 x 2 = 36 members, 72 with both read-outs; GBM 16 x 2 x 2 = 64 members.
findings.suggested_ruling: §3.5 as written replaces the words "same 3-init averaging" of LEAD_DECISIONS: MDN_B has 10 initialisations with both read-outs as family members, each GBM member is a 3-seed bag and the selected one a 9-seed bag, each seed unit is compared with the full comparator, and no comparator ensemble may be reduced later.

points.recommendation: Add the val-cell scenes to the reference set (fit + inner + val) and fix this now.
points.reason: v2, every comparator family member, the conformal offsets and the MDE inputs are chosen on validation rows, so a scene shared with validation is not unseen for selection. The AquaCorr preview still passes (2,402 of 3,790 rows, 63.4%; 153 of 169 blocks, 90.5%), but the margin is thin and WQP reference scenes will lower it. If the 60/80 rule then fails, the roles swap as written and the report must say the primary cell is not scene-disjoint. Deciding before the WQP counts exist removes a count-dependent choice.

points.recommendation: Accept rule now, status later, but only with the calculation fixed now as in finding MDE-SPEC and the thresholds declared final.
points.reason: Validation predictions of new targets cannot exist before the stamp, so the status cannot be computed today. The remaining freedom lies in the arm, the validation rows, the simulation settings and the Holm divisor; all can be fixed in one ruling.

points.point: 3. Context date limit and two-sided context (§3.4 item 3)
points.recommendation: Accept the limit of 2023-12-31 and the two-sided context. Make the scope sentence mandatory wherever an A1 or v2 result is reported, the event results of §6.3 included: retrospective reconstruction, uses later images of the same lake, no nowcast claim. Keep the stratum context >= 1 date versus none.
points.reason: The limit keeps headline-year imagery out of development and Test-S. A two-sided context cannot be used in real time, so an unscoped result would overstate operational skill.

points.recommendation: Accept as written and record that it replaces the lead's words "same 3-init averaging"; forbid any later reduction.
points.reason: It is the stricter reading. A 3-initialisation MDN_B would be weaker than the published method (10), and the reported candidate has 9 networks. It is still a deviation in letter, so it needs the lead's explicit sentence.

points.recommendation: Keep it. Out-of-fold features come from the fit cell only, in folds grouped by role block; every member is counted.
points.reason: Rule 3 requires the same auxiliary targets for the references. The member can only strengthen the baseline, and it is declared before any result.

points.point: 6. Track N arm when v2 = A0 or when A1 fails (§2.7)
points.recommendation: Accept as written. Add that the A1 configuration scored on Track N is chosen by validation chl-a only, never by a Track N validation number, and that it is not a third arm in H1-S.
points.reason: The rule is fixed before any result. If A1 fails its kill criterion no SENTINEL claim is made on Track N, which is the conservative outcome. Holm for H1-S stays over 2 arms.

points.point: 7. Shared initialisation fixed when A0 starts (§3.1)
points.recommendation: Stricter than the default: no A0 or A1 network starts before the v1 dev_v5 selection (protocol §6, §6a and §11.6) is registered and written into a regenerated v1 freeze candidate; the recipe is recorded by that file's sha256.
points.reason: The start moment is chosen by the author, so it could follow a chain9 result. §3.3 also defines A0 as the frozen headline recipe; a later change of v1 would break the A0 - v1 attribution (finding INIT-A0).

points.recommendation: Accept the default: fine-tuning auxiliary head only, GLORIA pretraining unchanged, dropped by the count rule (< 200 fit values), descriptive.
points.reason: Changing pretraining would change the initialisation shared with A0 and v1 and confound attribution. The WQP table has only 5,996 aCDOM rows in total, so the count rule may drop the head; counts decide, not results.

points.recommendation: Apply the MDE > 15 rule to Secchi, TSS and NTU as well, and keep the Holm divisor at 6 whatever is declared descriptive. The turbidity endpoint uses NTU-class rows only.
points.reason: Rule 1 requires power for a confirmatory family and none is given. The dev_v4 counts (92 and 49 rows) cannot support a confirmatory claim, and the plan's own table calls them descriptive. A fixed divisor removes any gain from a status set after validation.
No model receives it, so parity holds without further rules. Adding it later would need its own stamped addendum before any validation number.

points.recommendation: Agree, with the rulings of TESTLOOK-IMPORT, FROZEN-SET and POWER-SCRIPT.
points.reason: New modules outside the v1 hash protect the v1 candidate. But the hashed set is 43 files, not four globs, and the look-specific guard code and the power script cannot be reused without either editing v1 files or re-implementing them.

points.point: 12. Early stopping on four base targets; a-priori valid ranges (§3.4 item 9, §2.1)
points.recommendation: Agree. The ranges are fixed now and are not revised after any value is seen; out-of-range values are set missing and counted per target.
points.reason: Stopping on the base targets keeps A1's stopping rule equal to A0's and v1's, so new-target validation cannot steer training length. Ranges fixed before any label value is read leave no choice after results.

points.point: G1. Track G draft: Test-S interaction (G-A1 item 5)
points.recommendation: Accept. Archive-year G1-G5 rows of test-role lakes are counted by key and left unused once M2S/test is sealed; in either order they are never used for training or tuning.
points.reason: Adding rows to a sealed look would reopen it, and training on them would break the Test-S reservation.

points.point: G2. Track G draft: v2 = c1 (G-A2)
points.recommendation: Keep c2 as the single Track-G configuration whenever v2 is an A1 configuration, and do not refit or score c1 on Track G. Reword G-A4 to match and state in reports that c2 was not the selected v2.
points.reason: The plan (line 666) and the amendment (line 328) already name c2. The amendment defines no coordinates-off output for c1 (no coordinate dropout), so the alternative would need a design change after the stamp. The draft as written scores two configurations under a cap of 1.

points.point: G3. Track G draft: data version name
points.recommendation: Name it when Track G is funded, in the funding ruling; until then the texts say "the Track-G data version". Update the GPU and seed wording of orbit_track_g.md in the same step.

summary: Hash matches. No validation number, run folder or registry row exists for any new arm or Track N target; all cited counts match the keys-only JSON. No blocking finding; fourteen should_fix items, each closable by one ruling. Most urgent: a stale ABORTED.json, written by a unit test into the real M2/test look directory, would spend the v1 headline look at claim time. Others: "imported, never copied" and the orbit_power.py re-run both require v1-hashed files; the hashed set is 43 files, not four globs; kNN power is omitted (33.7 points at 87 blocks); MDE status rules leave choices open; parity wording deviates (stricter) from the lead's; the A0 start time and kill-criterion reference are not fixed.
